candidates.statement: This guidance does not address use of growth or pubertal development data to support primary 24 evidence of efficacy in growth disorders (e.g., primary growth deficiency, disorders of pubertal 25 development such as precocious puberty or delayed puberty). Sponsors should further discuss 26 with the appropriate review division how to establish efficacy for such drugs. 2
candidates.context: This guidance is intended to assist sponsors in monitoring growth and, when appropriate, 19 pubertal development in clinical trials that enroll pediatric participants with rare and common 20 diseases. This guidance provides recommendations for the most appropriate methods for 21 measuring and recording growth and evaluating pubertal development for evaluation of safety. 22 This guidance does not address evaluation of nutritional status. This guidance does not address 29 statistical methods for analyzing growth or pubertal developmental data. 30

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 32 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 33 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 34 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 35 not required. 36

candidates.statement: In general, pediatric clinical trials should include accurate, serial measurements and recordings 41 of growth parameters if an investigational drug has the potential to affect growth or pubertal 42 development. Typically, growth is assessed using measurements of weight and linear growth 43 (length and height), and when appropriate, head circumference. Additional measurements and 44 calculations may be needed in certain pediatric age groups and disease populations, as discussed 45 further in section III., Measurements of Growth and Pubertal Development. Typically, pubertal 46 development is assessed using clinical phenotyping. Accurately identifying the onset and 47 progression of puberty is essential for accurate interpretation of growth data. 48
candidates.context: III. MEASUREMENTS OF GROWTH AND PUBERTAL DEVELOPMENT 51

candidates.statement: Sponsors should consider the following for measuring growth in pediatric participants enrolled in 57 clinical trials: 58
candidates.context: 1. General Considerations 55 • Develop a protocol for training investigators and trial site personnel responsible for 60 collecting growth parameters and conducting physical examinations and include 61 procedures for determining a trial participant’s age, obtaining growth measurements, 62 instrument calibration, and evaluation of pubertal development. 63

candidates.statement: • In general, collect and record growth measurements for a minimum trial duration of 12 70 months. Sponsors should discuss alternative trial durations with the appropriate review 71 division and consider any potential safety concerns related to the drug for the intended 72 patient population. 73
candidates.context: • Avoid self-reported growth measurements because they may not be sufficiently accurate, 65 consistent, and reliable for data collection. Growth measurements assessed outside of 66 established trial sites may be acceptable if the measurements are taken by a trained health 67 care professional using appropriate and calibrated instruments. 68 • Keep pediatric participants who discontinue the study treatment in the trial to continue to 75 obtain their growth measurements. Measurements obtained after treatment 76 discontinuation may be useful for ensuring the reliability and interpretability of analyses 77 and results. 78

candidates.statement: To reduce measurement error, the sponsor should include procedures and practices in the 82 protocol, such as the following: 83
candidates.context: a. Reducing measurement error 80 • Outline procedures for calibration of measuring instruments (e.g., calibration timing 85 relative to measurement, calibration frequency). 86

candidates.statement: • For trials involving multiple treatment arms, blind trial site personnel to each trial arm. 93 For single-arm trials, the sponsor should discuss with the appropriate review division 94 how the trial could be designed to avoid biased measurement of growth parameters. 95
candidates.context: • Document how measurements are obtained (e.g., for weight, use of tared weight, 88 documenting type of scale, clothing; for height, use of recumbent or standing methods of 89 measurement) and how to address challenges in obtaining measurements (e.g., 90 uncooperative child, assistive technology). 91 • Because of diurnal variations in height and weight, schedule study visits and/or perform 97 growth measurements at the same time of day unless justification is provided. 98

candidates.statement: Appropriately determining a participant’s age is important for accurate and consistent 102 documentation of growth. Sponsors should consider the following when determining age: 103
candidates.context: • For participants 3 years of age and older, calculate and use the chronological age to the 105 nearest month and year. 106

candidates.statement: Sponsors enrolling pediatric participants in clinical trials should consider incorporating the 169 following considerations in the trial protocol regarding weight assessment: 170
candidates.context: • Use a scale with an electronic (i.e., digital) reading that allows for adjusting the scale to 172 zero prior to weighing the pediatric participant. 173

candidates.statement: Sponsors should consider the following for measuring length and height in pediatric participants 230 enrolled in clinical trials: 231
candidates.context: 3. Linear Growth (Length and Height) Assessment 228 • Measure recumbent length in participants from birth to less than 2 years of age using a 233 length board (or infantometer) with a fixed head piece, horizontal backboard, and an 234 adjustable foot piece. The length board should be placed on a flat, stable surface. 235

candidates.statement: • Measure recumbent length in participants from birth to less than 2 years of age using a 233 length board (or infantometer) with a fixed head piece, horizontal backboard, and an 234 adjustable foot piece. The length board should be placed on a flat, stable surface. 235
candidates.context: Sponsors should consider the following for measuring length and height in pediatric participants 230 enrolled in clinical trials: 231 • Measure standing height in participants 2 years of age and older using a stadiometer 237 mounted at a right angle between a level floor and against a straight, vertical surface. 238

candidates.statement: • Provide details in the protocol on any alternative strategies that will be used for 261 evaluating linear growth in trials enrolling pediatric participants with conditions that may 262 affect measurement of linear growth (e.g., contractures, genetic syndromes including 263 skeletal dysplasia, scoliosis). For participants who are not cooperative with linear growth 264 measurements, sponsors should consider an adjustment strategy based on 265 recommendations by WHO 11 or other professional health organizations. 266

candidates.statement: Sponsors should consider the following for measuring head circumference in pediatric 270 participants enrolled in clinical trials: 271
candidates.context: 4. Head Circumference Assessment 268 • Measure head circumference (HC) using a nonelastic tape measure. 273

candidates.statement: • Measure HC at the maximum diameter of the head (the glabella to the occiput) and to the 281 nearest 0.1 cm. Abnormal head shape (e.g. craniosynostosis, positional plagiocephaly, 282 microcephaly) should be documented. 283

candidates.statement: Sponsors enrolling pediatric participants in clinical trials should use a sexual maturity rating 309 (e.g., Tanner Staging) to evaluate and document pubertal development at baseline (i.e., trial 310 entry) and at regular intervals based on the potential safety concerns associated with the drug and 311 the pubertal development stage of the pediatric participant. Sponsors should also consider the 312 following: 313
candidates.context: B. Pubertal Development 307 • Discuss with the appropriate review division the appropriate intervals for evaluation of 315 pubertal development. 316

candidates.statement: • Sexual maturity ratings should be based on both breast and pubic hair changes in females 318 and on both genital and pubic hair changes in males. Evaluation of genital changes in 319 males should include an assessment of testicular volume using an orchidometer. 320
candidates.context: • Discuss with the appropriate review division the appropriate intervals for evaluation of 315 pubertal development. 316 • Discontinue or do not initiate pubertal development assessments when the participant has 322 completed puberty (i.e., Tanner 5). candidates.statement:  Train investigators and examiners on how to conduct sexual maturity ratings. 325 Whenever possible, the same trial health care professional should evaluate pubertal 326 development. 327
